observations.statement: Goal Mode is defined as a native autonomous, general-purpose execution mode rather than a prompt-packet, D2-style handoff, or planning-only feature; visible Assistant Chat and invisible Planning Wizard uses share the engine.

Goal Mode may self-initiate named web and browser operations when external or dynamic evidence matters; those calls use the shared dispatcher, record invocation provenance, obey effective network and permission policy, and render named visible operation states.

Goal Runtime owns runtime state, scheduling, update and replan semantics, authority, evidence, certification, role policy, and child-goal coordination, while Assistant Chat owns visible controls and projections and FinalGUISpec owns model-selection placement.

Ledger, Plan Document, and Plan-To-Node owners retain records, PlanUnits, generated indexes, and readiness-only compilation; Goal Runtime can consume them but cannot create executable implementation artifacts, and web or browser evidence remains source evidence until an explicit compile or build phase.

The ownership split assigns the global approval ladder to Permissions_System, Goal-specific high-risk invocation and invisible-goal blocking to Goal Runtime, runtime-artifact browsing to Runtime_Artifacts_Panel, and concrete provider identity to model and provider owners.
GRS-001 accepts arbitrary assistant goals, prohibits narrowing to planning transfer or prompt loops, and names plan-index validation plus manual owner review as its validation surfaces.

GRS-032 permits Goal Runtime to request, consume, and certify containerized-host-dependent work without direct host dispatch; host, execution-context, test, preflight, execution, cleanup, blocker, and Runtime Artifacts references cross Executor, testing, tools, and subagent boundaries.

Host-aware completion requires lane-appropriate evidence, an explicit blocker payload, or an approved verification exception; missing evidence fails or blocks certification, blocked host outcomes cannot become success, and Runtime Artifacts is not receipt authority.

GRS-002 requires one lifecycle model for invisible, visible Assistant Chat, and Orchestrator integrations; invisible goals are hands-off for ordinary ambiguity, defined hard-stop classes remain, and Executor retains readiness, backoff, capacity, and dispatch authority.

GRS-003 makes Planning Wizard and PRD Builder ledger-first, allows invisible conversion only after readiness, provides three minimal status examples, rejects default WorkNode treatment, and requires explicit Orchestrator handoff with lineage, readiness evidence, and Goal Runtime receipts.
Context-only GRS-004 begins a whole-task-coherence requirement for sharded inputs and says sharding is retrieval and verification infrastructure rather than D2-style execution slicing.

candidate_findings.title: Shared lifecycle is asserted without an exact state machine
candidate_findings.statement: The core assigns durable state, scheduling, update and replan semantics, and child-goal coordination to Goal Runtime and requires one shared lifecycle, but it does not enumerate goal states, transition preconditions, persisted fields, ordering, concurrency, idempotency, recovery, or child-to-parent transition rules.
candidate_findings.impact: Independent integrations can implement incompatible state machines, lose durable progress, race updates, or disagree about terminal and recoverable states while each appears to satisfy the prose.

candidate_findings.title: Web self-initiation and operation outcomes lack decision semantics
candidate_findings.statement: The trigger is only that evidence 'matters', and the core lists progress, partial, denied, fallback, approval, session, and unavailable cards without defining source-sufficiency thresholds, mandatory versus optional calls, timeout or retry behavior, fallback ordering, or which outcomes block completion.
candidate_findings.impact: Builders can make materially different research decisions and can treat partial, denied, or unavailable evidence inconsistently, producing non-reproducible goals and misleading completion.

candidate_findings.title: Goal approval and predeclared-authority boundaries are not operationally defined
candidate_findings.statement: The core requires explicit approval for high-risk actions and blocking outside predeclared authority but does not define high-risk classes, authority declaration shape, approval granularity and actor, denial behavior, persistence, expiry, or unblock and resume transitions.
candidate_findings.impact: The same action can be silently allowed, repeatedly deadlocked, or presented for approval differently across integrations, undermining both safety and autonomous completion.

candidate_findings.title: Host capability and receipt references have no interoperable data contract
candidate_findings.statement: GRS-032 names many references that must cross Executor, testing, tools, and subagent boundaries, but the core does not specify their types, requiredness, cardinality, producer, consumer, correlation keys, versioning, validation, or stale and duplicate handling.
candidate_findings.impact: Goals can attach the wrong host or test evidence, omit required fields without deterministic rejection, or fail to exchange receipts across subsystem boundaries.

candidate_findings.title: Blocked, failed, and completion-certification outcomes are ambiguous
candidate_findings.statement: Missing host evidence is allowed to 'fail or block' certification, while an explicit blocker payload can satisfy the stated certification prerequisite and blocked must not become success; the core gives no deterministic decision table, terminality rule, retry or resume transition, timeout, or receipt result shape.
candidate_findings.impact: Implementations can disagree on whether the same evidence yields failure, a resumable block, a terminal non-success receipt, or accidental successful completion.

candidate_findings.title: Verification exceptions can bypass evidence without defined authority
candidate_findings.statement: Completion certification permits approved verification exceptions, but the core does not name the approving authority, eligible lanes and reasons, minimum substitute evidence, scope, expiry, revocation, persistence, or audit fields.
candidate_findings.impact: A builder can turn the exception path into an unconstrained bypass of host, test, or cleanup evidence and issue false completion certification.

candidate_findings.title: Completion-receipt and evidence identity semantics are claimed but not specified
candidate_findings.statement: Goal Runtime expressly owns completion receipt semantics and evidence identity requirements, yet the core supplies no receipt schema, identifier rules, uniqueness or deduplication behavior, evidence binding and hashing rules, persistence lifecycle, or validation oracle.
candidate_findings.impact: Completion receipts can be unverifiable, duplicated, rebound to the wrong goal or execution, or inconsistently retained and projected.

candidate_findings.title: Stop and hard-stop classes lack cancellation and cleanup behavior
candidate_findings.statement: GRS-002 lists explicit user stop and other hard stops, and the authority statement includes child goals, but the core does not define in-flight cancellation, propagation to children, atomicity, host or tool cleanup, late-result handling, completion receipts, restart, or resume semantics.
candidate_findings.impact: Stopped goals can leave orphaned child work or resources, accept late side effects, or surface inconsistent final status and evidence.

candidate_findings.title: Hands-off ambiguity and true-blocker classification leave consequential discretion
candidate_findings.statement: Invisible goals must continue through ordinary ambiguity but stop for contradictory goal text and true blockers; the core does not define ordinary ambiguity, contradiction, true infrastructure blocker, precedence among hard-stop classes, or escalation when classifications conflict.
candidate_findings.impact: One implementation can guess through a dangerous ambiguity while another blocks routine work, defeating consistent hands-off behavior.

candidate_findings.title: Model-role and weak-model certification policy is absent
candidate_findings.statement: The core claims ownership of weak-model safety, verifier and adjudicator policy, role-policy usage, and certification tiers, but it does not define role assignment, model qualification, worker-verifier separation, fallback, quorum, disagreement, adjudication, or tier-to-evidence rules.
candidate_findings.impact: Builders can permit self-certification, use an underqualified model for a safety-critical role, or resolve evaluator disagreement without a reproducible authority rule.

candidate_findings.title: Planning readiness and explicit handoff have no transaction contract
candidate_findings.statement: GRS-003 allows conversion 'After readiness' and requires an explicit Orchestrator handoff, but the core does not identify the readiness authority and oracle, required version or snapshot, initiating actor, payload schema, acknowledgement, idempotency key, duplicate handling, rollback, or handoff failure state.
candidate_findings.impact: Conversion can start against unready or stale ledger state, and repeated or partially failed handoffs can create divergent graph-preparation work.

candidate_findings.title: Validation surfaces do not provide executable behavior oracles
candidate_findings.statement: The PlanUnits rely on plan-index validation, manual review, and future lifecycle, fixture, or integration checks; the core gives no current fixture schema, expected state traces, negative cases, or executable assertions for runtime, host-certification, hard-stop, or handoff behavior.
candidate_findings.impact: Structural plan validation can pass while incompatible or unsafe runtime behavior remains untested and uncertified.

candidate_findings.title: Runtime-to-GUI projections and controls lack consistency guarantees
candidate_findings.statement: Assistant Chat is to display Goal Runtime status and expose pause, resume, stop, and update controls, and visible and Orchestrator integrations expose controls through owner surfaces, but the core does not define projection freshness, ordering, optimistic versus acknowledged command state, command rejection, reconnect reconciliation, or stale-state indication.
candidate_findings.impact: The GUI can display a status that disagrees with durable runtime truth or report a control action as effective before the runtime accepts it.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: The product-scope boundary is explicit: Goal Mode is native, general-purpose, and must not be rebuilt as a prompt-packet, D2 slice workflow, planning-only assistant, or prompt loop.
The compile boundary is explicit: Goal Runtime may consume planning contracts but does not create WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, final node manifests, or production build tasks.
Web and browser artifacts used during planning flows are explicitly source evidence only and cannot create implementation work or runtime dispatch by themselves.

Host authority and success boundaries are explicit: Goal Runtime cannot dispatch host work directly, blocked host outcomes cannot be transformed into success, and Runtime Artifacts is projection rather than receipt truth.
The three product integrations are explicitly required to share one lifecycle, and Orchestrator projections explicitly cannot replace Executor readiness, backoff, capacity, or dispatch authority.
Invisible goals explicitly avoid row-by-row and ordinary-ambiguity questioning while retaining hard stops for authority, safety, missing preconditions, user stop, contradiction, and true blockers.

The Planning Wizard boundary is explicit: structured ledger capture precedes invisible conversion, conversational PRD work is not a Goal or WorkNode by default, and any Orchestrator handoff carries lineage, readiness evidence, and receipts.

GUI ownership is explicitly split: Assistant Chat owns visible controls and projections, FinalGUISpec owns model-selection placement, and concrete Planning Wizard layout, copy, and screen behavior is routed out of Goal Runtime canon.
Legacy Chain Wizard and Requirements Doc Builder names are explicitly retained only as compatibility and source-lineage aliases and are retired as current terminology.

unknowns.statement: The exact imported behavior of Contracts_V0, Assistant Chat, Planning Ledger, Plan Document, and Plan-To-Node Compilation cannot be determined because only their references are present in the assigned window.
The meanings and contracts of GRS-032 dependencies EP-109, RM-048, T-166, ATS-019, RAP-042, and CV-303 and unblocked units OSI-431, OP-028, and RGV-015 cannot be determined from this window.
Executor's concrete readiness, backoff, capacity, dispatch, and Goal Runtime projection interfaces are outside the assigned core and therefore cannot be verified.
The actual current existence and behavior coverage of the named future lifecycle tests, host-evidence fixture, and Planning Wizard integration review cannot be verified within the permitted sources.

Concrete Planning Wizard status-to-state mapping, accessibility behavior, localization, screen layout, and copy beyond the three examples cannot be determined because the core explicitly routes those details to other owner docs.
Concrete provider and account identities and the worker and verifier/adjudicator settings behavior cannot be determined from this core because their ownership is assigned elsewhere.

Only the opening context lines of GRS-004 are in scope; any dependency list or later acceptance, validation, failure, and implementation details for its sharding requirement remain unknown and are not used to substantiate a core finding.

exact_evidence_refs.exact_quote: > **Authority:** Canonical owner for native Goal runtime/control-plane behavior, invisible and visible goal execution, durable goal state, scheduler updates, evidence, completion receipts, child goals, weak-model safety, verifier/adjudicator policy, goal authority boundaries, and runtime-facing Goal Mode task templates.

The Goal Runtime System is Puppet Master's native autonomous execution mode for long-running, cross-referential, or multi-step work. It is not a prompt-packet workflow, not a D2-style staged handoff, and not a planning-only assistant feature.

Goal Mode is general-purpose: user-facing Assistant Chat can invoke it for bugs, features, tests-until-pass, refactors, documentation, repository research, migrations, audits/repairs, and planning/doc transfer. Internal product flows such as future Planning Wizard ledger-to-Plans transfer use the same engine invisibly; legacy Chain Wizard transfer references are compatibility/source-lineage aliases only.

Goal Mode may self-initiate `websearch`, `webfetch`, `webextract`, `webresearch`, `deep_research`, `webcrawl`, `webmap`, and Site Reader / BrowserAction evidence when current, external, URL, visual, dynamic-page, docs/issues/PR, comparison, research, or deep-research evidence matters. These calls go through the shared PM WebOperation/BrowserAction dispatcher, record `invocation_source` and `agent_reason`, obey the effective permission/no-network/egress policy, and render visible operation, progress, partial, denied, fallback, source, approval, session, or unavailable cards in the owning surface.

Goal Runtime owns runtime state, scheduling, update/replan semantics, authority, evidence, certification, model-role policy, and child-goal coordination.

Assistant Chat owns the visible chat controls and displays that project Goal Runtime state: activation, status chips, task trackers, pause/resume/stop/update controls, activity/evidence cards, completion summaries, and collapsible child-goal detail.
FinalGUISpec owns GUI placement for settings surfaces, including the two Goal Mode model selections for worker and verifier/adjudicator roles.

Planning Ledger, Plan Document, and Plan-To-Node docs remain owners for ledger records, PlanUnits, generated indexes, and the readiness-only compiler boundary. Goal Runtime may consume those contracts for ledger-to-Plans goals, but it does not create WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, final node manifests, or production build tasks.

When Goal Runtime is invoked by PRD Builder, Planning Wizard, Chain Wizard compatibility flows, or ledger-to-Plans transfer, web/browser evidence is source evidence only until an explicit compile/build phase. Read receipts, extract receipts, citations, browser artifacts, and research closure states may flow into ledger records, PRD source refs, PlanningRun evidence, PlanUnit source lineage, or Goal receipts, but they do not create implementation work or runtime dispatch by themselves.

Permissions_System owns the global approval ladder and rule resolution. Goal Runtime owns the Goal-specific invocation rule: high-risk goal actions request explicit approval and invisible/internal goals block when outside predeclared authority.
Runtime_Artifacts_Panel owns user-visible runtime-artifact browsing and retention UI. Goal Runtime owns completion receipt semantics and evidence identity requirements.

Prompt_Pipeline, Models_System, Multi-Account, Provider docs, and provider-specific integration docs own concrete provider/model/account identity. Goal Runtime owns role-policy usage: worker, planner, evaluator, verifier, and adjudicator roles and certification-tier requirements.

Goal Mode is a native autonomous execution mode for finished Puppet Master product behavior. It replaces the failed long prompt-packet/D2 handoff approach for long or cross-referential work. It must support arbitrary assistant goals and must not be narrowed to planning-doc transfer, bootstrapped PM Goal Mode, prompt loops, or staged prompt packets under a different name.

This addendum compiles containerized-host Goal Runtime consumption obligations from bootstrap ledger `pldg-20260630-001-feature-intake`. It does not create WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, implementation files, runtime dispatch, production build tasks, generated governance artifacts, or a governance seal.

Goal Runtime may request, consume, and certify work that depends on containerized-host capability, but it does not
  dispatch host work directly and cannot treat blocked host state as completion evidence. Goals, child goals, and
  verification or repair cycles pass host_capability_ref, host_profile_id, host_assignment_id, execution_unit_context_ref,
  TestRunReceipt refs, host_preflight_receipt, host_execution_receipt, cleanup_retention_receipt, blocked_reason_code, and
  Runtime Artifacts evidence refs through Executor, Automated Testing, Tools, and subagent boundaries. Goal completion
  certification requires lane-appropriate host/test/cleanup receipts, explicit blocker payloads, or approved verification
  exceptions; Runtime Artifacts remains projection and evidence browsing, not receipt truth.

Goal Runtime uses one Goal Runtime engine with three product integrations labeled A. invisible, B. Goal mode exposed to the user in chat assistant, and C. orchestration flow: invisible internal goals for product flows, visible user-directed Goal mode in Assistant Chat, and Orchestrator Goal runtime flows that project GoalRun and WorkGraph state while delegating WorkNode readiness, backoff, capacity, and dispatch to Executor. Invisible goals are hands-off for ordinary ambiguity and continue from start to finish unless a hard stop, approval boundary, or true blocker applies. Hard-stop classes include explicit user stop, a forbidden specific action, missing source ledger, missing project plans or inaccessible target artifacts, permissions/file-system failure, unsafe/destructive scope, contradictory goal text, and true infrastructure blocker. Visible goals and Orchestrator goals expose controls and status through their owner surfaces while sharing the same runtime state and lifecycle model.

acceptance_criteria:
  - Invisible internal goals, visible Assistant Chat Goal mode, and Orchestrator Goal runtime flows share one lifecycle/state model.
  - The three integrations preserve the labels A. invisible, B. Goal mode exposed to the user in chat assistant, and C. orchestration flow.
  - Invisible goals do not ask row-by-row or ordinary ambiguity questions.
  - Hard stops remain available for authority, safety, missing preconditions, and true blockers.
  - Hard-stop classification preserves explicit user stop, missing source ledger, missing project plans, permissions/file-system failure, unsafe/destructive, and contradictory cases.
  - Orchestrator Goal runtime projections do not replace Executor readiness, backoff, capacity, or dispatch authority.

  - future Goal Runtime lifecycle tests

negative_constraints:
  - Do not create a separate invisible-goal lifecycle that diverges from visible Goal Mode.
  - Do not ask row-by-row or ordinary ambiguity questions during invisible internal goals.
  - Do not let Orchestrator projections become Executor scheduler truth.

Future Planning Wizard and PRD Builder flows use the v2 ledger system conversationally first, preserving exact user intent before any invisible Goal conversion runs. After readiness, invisible Goal Mode may convert the accepted ledger to requirements docs, Plans, or graph-preparation artifacts while the Planning Wizard UI stays minimal with statuses such as Updating plan docs, Building project plan graph, and Reconciling feature requirements. Conversational PRD Builder work is not a default Orchestrator WorkNode; any later Orchestrator handoff is explicit and carries ledger lineage, readiness evidence, and Goal Runtime receipts. Legacy Chain Wizard and Requirements Doc Builder references remain compatibility/source-lineage aliases only.

Goal Runtime must preserve whole-task coherence while operating over sharded ledgers, sharded Plans, document maps, manifests, compact state, and source/target universes. Shard-group focus carries the whole goal summary, current focus, full objective, full source set/source universe, full target set/target universe, inspected scopes, uninspected scopes, hash/version metadata, and owner/consumer coverage; workers may request more context through runtime retrieval for source shards, target docs, code files, logs, images, or tests. Sharding is access, recovery, and verification infrastructure; it is not D2-style workflow slicing and must not become the core execution model.
